traverses the same schema through the same production code. If a topic branch ever appears in
`backend/services/semantic_compilation/`, one of these two fixtures stops working — and
`test_semantic_compilation_generality.py` scans the production sources for both fixtures'

prompt: Across these two specimens, how does the branching divide, where does the interval break down, and what growth rule would produce a third?

theorist_payload.reading: Both specimens send up one dominant axis and divide off it, but they divide differently. In the first, side shoots leave the axis in opposed pairs, so that each division doubles the count and the whole plant reads as symmetrical about its own stem. In the second, shoots leave singly and rotate around the axis, so no two neighbours face the same way and the plant reads as a spiral rather than a mirror. In both, the interval between divisions is regular for most of the length and then shortens sharply near the growing tip, where the divisions crowd together and the pattern is hard to read at all.

observables.kind: the extent of the dominant axis
observables.success_when: one extent is returned running the length of the specimen
observables.ambiguous_when: two extents of similar length come back and neither dominates
observables.refused_when: no instrument can be handed the phrase
observables.remains_interpretive: whether dominance is a matter of length at all

observables.kind: the angle at which each side element leaves the axis
observables.success_when: an angle is recovered for each element and the angles fall into two opposed groups
observables.ambiguous_when: the angles are continuous rather than grouped
observables.refused_when: the elements cannot be separated from the axis
observables.remains_interpretive: whether opposed pairs and a tight spiral are different rules or one rule at two rates

alternatives.label: measure each element's departure angle
alternatives.consequence: an angle per element; precise, and it needs every element separated first

alternatives.label: recover an orientation field over the whole specimen
alternatives.consequence: no element separation needed, and the answer is a tendency rather than a set of angles

observables.kind: the spacing between successive divisions along the axis
observables.success_when: spacings are recovered and are near-constant over most of the run
observables.ambiguous_when: the divisions cannot be ordered along the axis
observables.refused_when: fewer than three divisions are found

observables.kind: the departure pattern in each image, compared
observables.success_when: both images return a pattern and the two patterns differ in kind
observables.ambiguous_when: one image returns a pattern and the other returns nothing
observables.remains_interpretive: whether a difference in kind is a difference in rule

observables.kind: a documented name for the arrangement
observables.success_when: a citation is returned that names the arrangement
observables.remains_interpretive: whether this specimen belongs to the class the source describes

observables.kind: a reading of the specimen's character
observables.success_when: a reading is produced and is labelled as a reading
observables.remains_interpretive: all of it. A reading about a picture is never evidence in it.

decisions.question: Measure a departure angle for each element, or recover an orientation field over the whole specimen?
decisions.why_now: the first needs every element separated before anything can be measured; the second needs none of that and answers a tendency rather than the per-element question the claim actually makes

options.label: measure each element's departure angle
options.consequence: per-element angles, if the elements can be separated at all

options.label: recover an orientation field over the whole specimen
options.consequence: a tendency, available even where elements overlap, and not the claim as stated

semantic_remainder.why: departure angles and spacings both bear on it and neither settles it; nothing returns a number for whether a plant reads as a spiral
the prompt's distinction is about what to count as an event, and no instrument is scoped to a definition
